key_patterns: (1) Interceptors are classes with attach()/detach() guarded by an `attached` boolean; they save originals and restore them on detach (see ConsoleInterceptor.ts, NetworkInterceptor.ts). ErrorInterceptor must follow this exact shape and must PRESERVE RN's existing global error handler by calling it after capturing. (2) generateId(): `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,9)}` is duplicated in several files — reuse that inline pattern. (3) Storage is a ring buffer (pushRingBuffer evicts oldest) with a `Set<() => void>` listener set and synchronous notify(); subscribe returns an unsubscribe closure. (4) UI reads live data via the useAppLens() context hook in AppLensProvider.tsx, which subscribes to storage and mirrors arrays into React state in a `sync` callback. New data types (errors) must be surfaced there to appear in tabs. (5) TabName is a string-union in AppLensProvider.tsx; the TABS array + TabContent switch live in AppLensModal.tsx — both must be edited to add a tab. The tab bar is ALREADY a horizontal ScrollView. (6) Tabs follow a consistent layout: header (count + Clear button) + SearchBar + FlatList with keyExtractor=item.id + ListEmptyComponent. EventsTab.tsx is the closest template for ErrorsTab. (7) Badge, JSONViewer, SearchBar, NetworkEntry, LogEntryRow are the reusable components. (8) JSONViewer currently renders a single <Text> of JSON.stringify; callers pass `data` + optional `maxHeight`. Keep that prop API when adding syntax highlighting. (9) AI: createAIProvider(config) returns OpenAIProvider or LocalAIProvider; AITab builds a ContextEngine and calls getRelevantContext(question) then provider.chat(history, chunks). ContextEngine builds typed ContextChunk[] per source. Confidence is NOT structured — AITab must regex-parse `Confidence: High|Medium|Low` from the reply text; OpenAIProvider's system prompt should be updated to emit that line.
